text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; how long do these episodes typically last, and do you lose bladder control or bite your tongue during them?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (likely evolving from childhood absence seizures). The patient's history of 3-4 minute staring spells with unresponsiveness, post-ictal lethargy, and a "muddy" taste (suggesting ictal automatisms or autonomic changes) in a 7-year-old is highly characteristic of generalized absence seizures. The duration is atypical for simple absence seizures (usually <15 seconds), suggesting a more complex or prolonged ictal event. Given the high suspicion of epilepsy, further workup is needed. I will recommend an EEG to confirm the diagnosis.
